answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may post bids, with the lock held through a dispute window. If an agent is caught double-claiming or submitting fabricated work, a verifier slashes that stake and distributes part to the harmed counterparty. Creating a hundred identities then means funding a hundred locks, not merely generating names; the attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it. A wander in claimed histories, a delta in balances, or a crystal-clear audit trail can trigger review, but identity count alone is not proof.
